.. 
The main focus continues to be on Typhoon Champi, which continues to
strengthen. Champi began Rapid Intensification earlier this morning,
and appears like it could be going through an Eyewall Replacement 
Cycle, as there's been a couple of expansions and contractions where 
the eye's Central Dense Overcast (CDO), allowing the eye to become 
more opaque. This has been preceded by many lightning bursts that 
have mainly been confined to the southern flank of the eyewall, as 
one would expect.

Guam:
The Typhoon Warning remains in effect. Maximum sustained winds have
increased to 100 mph near the center, and it's forecast to continue
strengthening, with sustained winds of 115 mph probable late this
evening. At this time, Champi looks to pass over the southern tip of
Guam or just south between 4 AM and 6 AM, which will allow the storm
to continue to intensify as it moves through. The worst conditions
look to occur over the southern half of the island, where peak
sustained winds of 110 to 130 mph, with gusts to 160 mph, will be
possible. Winds will increase this evening, becoming strong tropical
storm force. Typhoon force winds are expected early Sunday morning.
These winds will continue to veer to the southwest, decreasing
through the afternoon. Damaging winds will continue into Sunday
night. 

Significant coastal flooding of up to 7 feet is expected, with 
landslides possibly causing road closures, especially south of Cross
Island Road.

Rota:
Sustained tropical storm force winds will move into the area this
evening, becoming strong tropical storm force by morning. However, 
if the typhoon "wobbles" far enough north, typhoon winds would 
potentially occur. As such, the Typhoon Warning remains in effect.

Tinian and Saipan:
Sustained tropical storm force winds are anticipated later tonight. 
These winds will develop after 7 PM, peaking between 3 AM and 9 Am 
when they become east- southeasterly. During this time, sustained 
withs of 40 to 50 mph, with gusts to 70 mph.

For more information, please reference our Zone Forecast package and
Typhoon Local Statement. 

As TY Champi departs the region, a dry pattern looks to move in, with
POPs (Probability of Precipitation) dropping to around 20 percent and
staying at these levels at least into next weekend.

Marine/Coastal...
Numerous roads may be closed. Low-lying property including homes, 
businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. 
Shoreline erosion will occur. Breaking waves can sweep people off 
their feet, and into dangerous seas. Life- threatening swimming 
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected. Coastal 
inundation of 5 to 7 feet for Guam, 2 to 4 feet for Rota and 1 to 3 
feet for Tinian and Saipan is possible along with coastal flooding 
and beach erosion.

Surf is expected to rise rapidly to dangerous levels tonight. 
Coastal impacts to the western coasts of Guam and Rota are highly 
dependent on the final track of Champi; passage south of Guam would 
be reduced impacts whereas passage over Guam would result in larger 
coastal inundation.

For more information please refer to the Hurricane Local Statement 
and Coastal Flood Warning.

Hydrology...
Typhoon Champi will produce locally heavy rainfall late tonight and 
Sunday. Although an unexpected southward shift in track will reduce 
these somewhat. Tinian and Saipan will see around 3 to 5 inches, Rota
could receive 5 to 8 inches, and Guam might get 8 to 14 inches. For 
more information please see the Flood Watch.

Tropical Systems...
As of 6:00 PM ChST, Typhoon Champi (29W) has rapidly intensified to
Category 4 with maximum sustained wind speeds of 130 MPH according
to the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC). Its center was located
around 12.5N 147.0E which was about 160 miles east-southeast of
Guam's radar and 200 miles south-southeast of Saipan airport. Champi
has slowed to 9 MPH heading west-northwest, with a forecast track
remaining south of Guam early Sunday morning as it intensifies 
further to a Super Typhoon within the next 12 hours. Environmental
conditions will be favorable for such strengthening characterized by
weak wind shear, warm sea surface temperatures, and exceptional
polar outflow. Over the past several hours, Champi has shifted its 
forward motion from west to west-northwest and slowed from 16 MPH to
9 MPH while increasing from Category 2 to Category 4 strength.
Typhoon-force winds are forecast to encompass all of Guam, with the
strongest impacts concentrated over southern Guam. However, should
the actual track shift more north, central and northern Guam could
see worse conditions. The onset of tropical-storm-force winds for all
of the Marianas is expected to occur imminently. Remain in sturdy
shelter and do NOT venture out.

For more information, please refer to the bulletins issued by the 
Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW, and by 
the National Weather Service in Tiyan, Guam under WMO header WTPQ32 
PGUM.

Eastern Micron
